title: PRD: Dynamic Overdraft Buffering and Usage Attribution for Multi-Plan Customers
creator: Sofia Martínez
description:
Problem: Some enterprise customers operate multiple plans (e.g., a core subscription + per-product add-ons) and spike on certain routes. Current behavior either (a) hard-enforces plan quotas and causes immediate failures when the primary quota is exhausted, or (b) silently charges overage with poor invoice traceability. Both outcomes create customer support load and erode confidence in plan semantics.

Objective: Deliver a predictable, auditable overdraft buffering mechanism that temporarily allows limited over-usage tied to a configurable buffer per-tenant and per-route, and that produces clear usage attribution and invoice-able reconciliation records. The feature should reduce operational incidents, improve invoice clarity, and enable safe graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.

Non-goals: This PRD does not change pricing tiers or unit prices. It does not implement cross-tenant credit pooling. It also does not replace direct rate-limiting policies for security/event protection (e.g., abuse mitigation).

Primary use-cases:
- Large SaaS customer with multiple services under one account: burst exceeds primary plan quota for a short window but should be served and billed to the correct plan line item after reconciliation.
- Platform teams who need to test new feature rollouts without immediate hard-failures but with accurate post-hoc billing.
- Support teams requiring clear attribution to explain invoices and process disputes.
scope: Per-tenant overdraft buffer config (global and per-route overrides)
Temporary token-level allowance and soft-denial if buffer exhausted
Usage attribution engine that tags tokens to in-plan vs overdraft vs fallback buckets
Reconciliation feed for billing (daily deltas + invoice-ready line items)
Console UI: buffer status, historical overdraft events, per-route charge preview
Acceptable fallbacks: automatic throttling and optional HTTP 402/429 behavior when buffers depleted
out_of_scope: Realtime financial settlement (this is reconciliation + invoicing integration)
proposed_solution: Implement a three-tier usage classification with a short-lived overdraft buffer: (1) In-plan consumption: normal billing to plan; (2) Overdraft buffer: ephemeral allowance configurable per-tenant (absolute tokens or percentage of quota) and per-route; (3) Emergency fallback: if buffer exhausted apply configured degradation (throttle, 402, or model downgrade). Usage records emitted at request time with attributes {tenant_id, route, model, tokens, classification, timestamp, request_id}. Daily reconciliation job aggregates overdraft usage into invoice line items with clear attribution. Console surfaces both live buffer health and post-facto invoicing preview. Admin API for support teams to grant manual buffer extensions and to export dispute-ready CSVs.
api_and_contracts: POST /v1/usage/report - extended payload includes classification and buffer_token_flag
Webhook: billing/reconciliation/overdraft - daily delta payload to billing system
Console: per-tenant page that shows remaining buffer and historical events
acceptance_criteria: Feature flags: overdraft buffering hidden behind a feature flag per tenant; default off
Config: Admins can set global default buffer and override per-route via API and Console
Runtime: When primary quota exhausted, system allows requests up to buffer limit and marks usage as 'overdraft' in emitted usage records
Reconciliation: Daily job produces invoice-ready CSV with columns (tenant_id, date, route, tokens_in_plan, tokens_overdraft, unit_price, line_item_code)
Attribution: > 99% of overdraft events include route and request_id fields required for support investigations
Fallback: If buffer is exhausted, system enforces tenant-configured fallback (throttle or HTTP 402) within 5s of decision path
Console: Buffer health and last 30 days of overdraft events available in UI for tenants with the feature enabled
Billing integration: Billing receives and ingests webhook payloads in a staging environment; test invoices reflect overdraft line-items
Monitoring: New SLOs - <0.5% of requests impacted by unexpected classification errors; alerting for reconciliation job failures
Security: Overdraft admin API endpoints require existing tenant admin role and audit logs enabled
metrics_and_success: Support tickets related to invoice confusion for enabled tenants drop by 40% in first 90 days
False-positive overcharge dispute rate < 2% for overdraft line items
Average reconciliation latency < 2 hours for daily aggregates
% of customers with configured buffer > 0 after 30 days (adoption target) = 20% of invited enterprise customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overdraft used as a loophole to avoid committing to higher plans. Mitigation: buffers are time-limited and can be capped relative to committed quota; include billing limits and manual review triggers
Risk: High-cardinality events increase storage/ETL costs. Mitigation: sample non-overdraft traffic; only emit full payload for overdraft-tagged requests or a configurable sampling rate
Risk: Reconciliation mismatch between runtime and billing. Mitigation: daily checksum job and a small retention window for raw events to support audits
Risk: Abuse (automated spraying). Mitigation: integrate with rate-limit and anomaly detection to disable overdraft for flagged tenants
